Porsche Singer 911.blurb: Singer-reimagined 964 - a different market to everything else here.

world.label: 300+ built, ongoing
world.detail: Singer completed its 300th reimagined 911 in February 2024 and is still building. No later total has been published. Every Singer is built on a 1989-94 964 and titled by that year, so all are past the 25-year line.

world.label: 1,270 built

na.detail: 644 United States + 31 Canada, of 1,270 built. The last model year turns 25 in 2031, so until then these are the cars that can legally be registered here.

Ford GT (2005-2006).blurb: Supercharged 5.4 V8, six-speed - the Le Mans homage, 4,038 built.

world.label: 4,038 built
world.detail: Every first-generation Ford GT, from the 2004 pre-production cars to the end of the line on 21 September 2006: roughly 550 in 2004, nearly 1,900 in 2005 and just over 1,600 in 2006. Ford had planned 4,500.

na.label: ~3,900 for N. America
na.detail: 4,038 built less the roughly 129 European deliveries (101 to the mainland, 28 to the UK). Those are allocation figures rather than audited builds, hence the tilde; about 200 of the North American cars went to Canada.

Chevrolet Corvette C8 Z06 (no Z07/wing).note: New model, launched MY2023 - no 2020-22 values exist, so those years are blank and the chart index starts at 2023. Every year is BaT sold medians for non-Z07, no-wing cars (listing-page check) x 0.82 to a 30k-mile basis - BaT has no 30k+ Z06 sales yet; 0.82 is Cars.com's 30k+ vs under-5k-mile asking ratio (2026-11-07). The adopted 2026 value is half that BaT figure and half the asking evidence - Cars.com plus CorvetteForum classifieds asks, each scaled to 30k miles and x 0.86 for ask-to-sold. Projection is depreciation, not appreciation: base -6%/yr, bear -10%, bull -2%.
